notes: YEAR CHOICE: used 2026 (not 2025) because AR, unlike SH, has a fully confirmed, complete, official municipal-level dataset for 2026 already published: ar.ch's 'Steuerfüsse 2026 natürliche Personen' sheet (Stand 28.04.2026) gives the cantonal multiplier plus every one of the 20 political-municipality and Kirchgemeinde multipliers for 2026, and the 'Mehrjahresvergleich 2016-2026' table cross-confirms the cantonal figure (3.30 Einheiten, unchanged 2022-2026). BRACKET TABLE / GENUINELY SEPARATE MARRIED & SINGLE SCHEDULES: unlike SH (which uses one table plus a splitting divisor), AR's Steuergesetz Art. 39 defines two ENTIRELY SEPARATE statutory bracket tables — 'Verheiratetentarif' (for married-jointly-taxed couples, and for widowed/separated/divorced/single taxpayers who mainly support children or dependents in their household) and 'Alleinstehendentarif' (everyone else) — there is no splitting divisor or formula link between them; both tables above are transcribed directly, no derivation needed. INFLATION-INDEXED AMOUNTS: the Steuergesetz's own base figures are round numbers (e.g. Fr. 16'000 / Fr. 8'000 for the first bracket) which Art. 39a requires the Regierungsrat to adjust for cold progression whenever cumulative CPI rise since the last adjustment reaches 3.0%; the LAST such adjustment took effect 01.01.2024, and the resulting adjusted figures (Fr. 16'700 / Fr. 8'300 etc., as used in the bracket tables above) remain the ones in force through 2025 and 2026 per the Feb-2026 ESTV Kantonsblatt (no further adjustment triggered since 2024). TOP-BRACKET QUIRK — REGRESSIVE MARGINAL RATE (flag prominently, more unusual than SH's case): both AR tables state that for income ABOVE the top threshold (Fr. 417'200 married / Fr. 260'800 single) 'die Einkommenssteuer beträgt ... 2,60 Prozent des steuerbaren Einkommens' — i.e. a flat 2.60% of the WHOLE income. We verified this equals the average rate accumulated through all lower brackets at exactly that threshold (married: CHF 10'847.70 cumulative tax at 417'200 = 2.6001% average; single: CHF 6'780.20 at 260'800 = 2.6001% average), so — exactly as with SH — it continues smoothly as an ordinary marginal breakpoint with no notch, and is safe to model as the final row above. BUT note the crucial difference from SH: here the flat 2.60% top rate is LOWER than the immediately preceding bracket's marginal rate of 2.90% — i.e. the AR marginal-rate curve is NOT monotonically increasing, it peaks at 2.90% in the second-to-last bracket then DROPS to 2.60% for all income above the top threshold. Total CHF tax owed still never decreases (the average rate curve is flat, not the tax amount), but a developer building a generic 'marginal rate always increases' assumption into shared bracket-table code will get AR wrong — this genuine degressive-tail structure (an explicit design choice to cap the average rate for very high incomes) is exactly the kind of per-canton quirk that justifies AR's own code path. WEALTH TAX MARGINAL-VS-CLIFF AMBIGUITY: Art. 52 StG is phrased as 'Für Vermögen bis Fr. 250'000 beträgt die einfache Steuer 0,50 Promille. Für Vermögen über Fr. 250'000 beträgt die einfache Steuer 0,55 Promille' — i.e. it does NOT use the explicit 'für die weiteren Fr. X' marginal-bracket phrasing that Art. 39 (income) uses. We modeled it as a standard MARGINAL bracket (first 250k at 0.5‰, only the excess above 250k at 0.55‰) because that is the universal convention for this exact two-tier 'bis X / über X' phrasing pattern in Swiss cantonal per-mille wealth-tax law and avoids an implausible notch (a whole-sum reinterpretation would jump total tax by CHF 125 at the exact 250'000 crossing, a real but small cliff) — however, since the statute text itself is genuinely ambiguous on this point (no cliff-vs-marginal statement located, and no example computation found in the Kantonsblatt to confirm either way), this is flagged for a developer to double check against ar.ch's own online Steuerrechner before shipping. MULTIPLIER UNIT — CRITICAL, NOT A PERCENTAGE (flag prominently): AR expresses its Steuerfuss in 'Einheiten der einfachen Staatssteuer' (Art. 3 StG / Art. 1391 Kantonsblatt) — i.e. a FACTOR, not a percent. The cantonal value is 3.30 Einheiten for 2026, meaning cantonal tax = 3.30 x einfache Steuer, NOT 3.3% of it. Municipal and church multipliers use the same Einheiten convention (e.g. Herisau political multiplier = 4.10 Einheiten). A developer must apply these as tax * multiplier directly (no /100), unlike SH/most other cantons where cantonalMultiplier.value=79 means tax * 0.79. This is the single most important AR-specific implementation detail. CHURCH-PARISH / POLITICAL-MUNICIPALITY BOUNDARY MISMATCH: AR church parishes do not always align 1:1 with political municipality boundaries (a legacy of parish structures predating today's municipal boundaries) — 3 of the 20 municipalities (Lutzenberg, Stein, Wolfhalden) have residents split between TWO different Catholic (or, in Lutzenberg's case, reformed-vs-catholic-with-same-name) parishes at genuinely different rates, with no single 'the' municipal Catholic rate; these are recorded as null in AR_municipalities.json with both options given here rather than guessing: Lutzenberg Catholic — Thal-Lutzenberg parish 0.74 Einheiten OR Wienacht-Tobel parish 0.30 Einheiten; Stein Catholic — Teufen parish 0.46 Einheiten OR Haslen parish 0.56 Einheiten; Wolfhalden Catholic — Thal-Lutzenberg parish 0.74 Einheiten OR Heiden parish 0.45 Einheiten. All other 17 municipalities have one unambiguous reformed and one unambiguous Catholic rate, cross-verified via the identity (political multiplier + cantonal 3.30 + church multiplier = published total column) for every row of the source table. DISTRICTS: AR genuinely retains 3 active Bezirke (Hinterland, Mittelland, Vorderland) in the BFS municipality register, unlike SH — these ARE populated in AR_municipalities.json (unlike SH's null).
